title: Morocco Road Trip: Nicolas and Raphael's Twingo Adventure
text:
The ‍Twing Raid is⁣ an adventurous rally event that takes place in the magical ⁢landscapes of Morocco, combining elements of a raid and ‍a rallye. Participants drive Renault Twingo 1 models,⁢ iconic cars from the ‍1990s,​ across challenging terrains including the Atlas Mountains and the⁢ sahara desert. The event aims to provide an exceptional and emotionally rich experience for⁢ the participants while also being accessible and fun.
The Twing ⁢raid is not⁤ just about the adventure; it also has ⁣a solidarity aspect. The event involves crossing the Sahara with a ⁢focus ‍on delivering foodstuffs and school supplies to the ​children ​of the ⁤desert. This adds a meaningful dimension to the adventure, making it an unforgettable experience for the participants.
The second edition of ‍the Twing Raid is scheduled ⁢to take ​place from February ‌25 to march 6, ⁢2025. this⁢ event brings together around 250 crews, ⁢each equipped‌ with‌ a Renault Twingo of the first generation. Participants like Raphaël and Nicolas prepare their vehicles meticulously, sometimes even buying ‍a⁤ second Twingo to gather necessary parts and resell the ones they don’t need.
The duo, trained in ‌boilermaking, has⁢ the skills to work on the sheet metal but finds the mechanical aspects ⁤of preparing ‌the vehicle challenging. They spend hours planning and adjusting their vehicle to meet the precise specifications provided by the institution, frequently enough ‌working late into⁤ the ⁢night to ensure everything is perfect.
For more information about‌ the Twing Raid, you can visit the official website Twing Raid or read more about the event on Les Enjoliveuses ‍and⁤ Caradisiac .
An Epic Adventure: the Twingo Raid In ⁣a world where adventure often takes a ‌backseat to routine, two friends, Raphaël and Nicolas, are‌ gearing up for an ‍remarkable ‌journey. Their goal? To ⁢participate in the Le twing raid ,an event that promises an unforgettable experience from start to finish.
A Vehicle Ready for the⁢ Challenge The vehicle they will be using is ‌no ordinary car. With 290,000 km on‌ the clock , it has seen‌ its fair share of roads. But it’s not just the mileage that sets it apart. This⁣ trusty steed had to be adapted and given a‌ new look to meet‍ the demands of the raid. Thanks to the help of a friend, Julien Lefevre, who lent them his farm, they‍ were able⁤ to paint the bumpers even in the rain.
! The two friends are ready to embark. They have installed bucket⁣ type seats so that the trip is more comfortable.© awarl ⁢Normand / AB
Equipped with 20 liters of fuel and the⁢ same amount of water,⁢ two extinguishers, personal affairs, a toolkit, and spare parts, the car is ready to tackle ⁢any challenge that comes its ⁢way. The duo‌ also plans to carry⁣ ten kilos‍ of non-perishable ‍food and hygiene⁢ products,which will be donated to Restos du Coeur before⁤ their departure from Saint-Sébastien, Spain. Additionally, they will distribute five kilos of school supplies to schoolchildren in Morocco.
Creating an Association and Finding sponsors Preparing for such an adventure required ⁣more than just packing. Raphaël and Nicolas had to create their first association, Asso Roc 127 , a nod to their race number and their ⁢professional ‍baccalaureate in “realization of cauldroned works.” This association allowed them to‌ collect ⁣donations and approach companies and businesses‌ to find sponsors for their budget of ‍around €8,000.
“We were relentless, we have deposited about fifty files ⁤ and ⁤a dozen agreed to⁣ support us in a very ⁤generous way,” they​ said, recalling the stress they ‌experienced when they realized that Nicolas’ passport woudl no ​longer⁣ be valid at the time of the test. fortunately, Nicolas received his new ⁣passport just in time for the registration deadline.
The Adventure Begins Le twing raid is ⁢an event that takes place without a competitive spirit. Participants are⁣ free to follow the route independently, observing the hours but not racing against each ⁢other. Two steps​ will be navigated using a simple map and a compass, a GPS without GPS approach. Aside from the last two nights at the hotel, the participants plan to bivouac and expect to face fresh nights in the desert.
“We want to experience the adventure from A to Z,” they declared, eager to⁢ “get the sun.”

Interview with Nicolas⁢ and Raphaël: An Epic Expedition Editor: Can ​you tell us about the preparations⁣ for‍ your upcoming adventure, ⁣”Le Twing Raid” with Raphaël?
Nicolas: Yeah, ‌Raphaël and I have been preparing for this adventure since last summer. We teamed up to colect donations and approach companies to find sponsors‍ for our budget of around €8,000. ⁤We were relentless⁣ and ⁤managed to ⁣deposit⁤ about fifty files, ⁢with a dozen companies supporting us generously.
Editor: It must have ⁤been stressful, especially with the passport issue. How did you‍ manage that?
Raphaël: Absolutely, it was quite stressful. Just when we realized that Nicolas’ passport would no longer​ be valid, he managed to get his new​ passport⁢ just in time. ⁢We were very relieved to get that sorted out.
The Adventure Begins Editor: Can you describe what participants can expect during “Le Twing Raid”?
Nicolas: “Le Twing Raid” is‌ an event with ⁣a non-competitive spirit.Participants can follow the route independently, observing the hours but not racing against each other. It’s an adventure where two steps will be navigated ‍using a simple map and a compass—no GPS. We plan to bivouac and expect fresh nights in the​ desert.
Editor: What motivates you both to ‍undertake⁣ such an adventurous journey?
Raphaël: We ‌want‍ to experience the adventure from A to Z. the thrill of exploring, getting the ⁣sun, ​and the spirit of the journey are what excite us⁣ the most.
